[1;97mshells 1 — the shell is a program[0m

The shell reads the line you type, finds the program you named, runs
it, and shows what it printed. The shell is itself a program.

  [92mecho $BASH_VERSION[0m   [90m# the version of the shell running now[0m
  [92mps[0m                    [90m# one line is this shell, one is ps itself[0m

[92m$BASH_VERSION[0m is a [36mvariable[0m: a name that holds a value. The
shell swaps [92m$name[0m for its value before it runs the line.

Notice that [92mps[0m lists the shell next to the command you just ran.

[93m▶ Run both commands, then type [92mnext[93m.[0m
[95mnext[0m[90m ▸ go on[0m   [95mshow[0m[90m ▸ this screen again[0m   [95mprev[0m[90m ▸ back[0m   [95mquit[0m[90m ▸ save and leave[0m

[1;97mshells 2 — other shells exist[0m

Four shells you will meet:
  [92mbash[0m   common on Linux; the shell this tutor runs
  [92mzsh[0m    the default on current macOS
  [92mfish[0m   a shell with its own syntax, installed separately
  [92msh[0m     the minimal standard shell, used by scripts

Ask which of two are installed here:
  [92mcommand -v zsh fish[0m   [90m# one path per shell found[0m

[36mDifferent[0m: configuration syntax, prompt, completion.
[36mThe same[0m: the programs ([92mls[0m, [92mcat[0m), paths, pipes, redirection.

Notice that no output means that shell is not installed. That is normal.

[1;97mshells 3 — your login shell and this shell[0m

Your account has a [36mlogin shell[0m: the one a new terminal window
starts. It can differ from the shell running now.

  [92mecho $SHELL[0m          [90m# your login shell[0m
  [92mecho $BASH_VERSION[0m   [90m# the shell running now[0m

[92m$SHELL[0m comes from your account. It does not change when you start
another shell from inside it.

This tutor runs its lessons in Bash whatever your login shell is, so
every learner sees the same thing. The programs you practise here
behave the same under [92mzsh[0m.
